transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Smith, they... my family brought me in. It was because of what happened down at the county fair. See, I was supposed to be giving my talk, and I just climbed right up onto the tractor. It was a John Deere, one of those newer ones... beautiful machine. My granddad used to swear by International Harvester, said the green ones were just overpriced lawnmowers, but the dealership in town closed back in '98. 

Anyway, I was up there, and I kept jerking the controls around to show the crowd the new pattern. The pattern is real important, you know? You gotta think about soil compaction, especially with all the rain we had this past April. Mud was up to the axles. But I was showing them the pattern, and I just... I couldn't make myself stop. Even with all those people yelling at me to get down. The yelling just started sounding like the crows out in the south pasture, they get so loud right around dusk...
Over the past few weeks, have you felt like you had so much energy that you didn't need to sleep much, or felt like your thoughts were moving so fast you couldn't keep up with them?

Well, sleep... sleep's been a funny thing lately. Most nights, I reckon I just doze off for maybe two or three hours, sitting right there in my recliner. It's one of those La-Z-Boys, you know, the brown corduroy ones? Got it on sale over in Shelbyville back when the kids were still in high school. The lever on the side sticks a little, but it's comfortable enough. 

But yeah, two or three hours, or sometimes I don't shut my eyes at all. And the funny thing is, I'm up before the sun even thinks about rising, just feeling completely charged up. Ready to go out and work the whole place like nothing happened. I mean, there's always fencing to mend. The deer, they just push right through the wire down by the creek. You'd think a five-strand barbed wire would keep 'em out, but they find a way. My neighbor, Tom, he put up that high-tensile electric fence, cost him a fortune... but I just don't see the need to spend that kind of money when you can just get out there early and fix it yourself. You know?
Have you ever felt this way—with so much energy and needing so little sleep—at any other time in your life, perhaps months or years ago?

Well, let me think on that... you know, looking back over this past year or so, it feels like I've been running on that same high gear for a long time. I'd say these stretches where I'm just charged up, not sleeping, going nonstop... they've taken up about ten months out of the last year. 

Ten months is a long time to be running hot. It reminds me of back in '82 when we had that drought. The ground was so dry it cracked open like a jigsaw puzzle, and we were hauling water from the county line just to keep the cattle from dropping. Had this old Ford F-250, dual gas tanks, burned oil like nobody's business, but she pulled that water trailer every single day. The transmission finally gave out right in front of the feed store in town. Old man Miller came out, shook his head, and said, "You work a machine that hard without a rest, something's bound to snap." He was right about the truck, of course. We ended up having to rebuild the whole gearbox... took three weeks and cost more than the truck was worth, probably. But you do what you have to do when the cattle need water.
